name: Papyrus sheets
note: Rome has abundant supply from Egypt. Writing surface, not an invention.

name: Parchment sheets
note: Rome produces from animal skin. Durable, reusable, erasable, expensive.

name: Wax tablets
note: Wooden frames with wax layer. Reusable by heating. For notes, not archival.

name: Codex binding
note: Stacked pages sewn and bound. Replaces roll. Page finding is the real gain.

name: Scribal copying
note: Trained hand copying, one manuscript at a time. Elite control of knowledge.

name: Carbon ink
note: Lampblack or charcoal suspended in gum. For brush and reed pen on soft surfaces.

name: Seals and stamps
note: Hand-carved into stone, metal or bone. Verify identity and authenticity.

name: Mosaic and fresco
note: Permanent architectural image. Tesserae or pigment in plaster. Not reproducible.

name: Sculpture
note: Stone or bronze permanent image. Single work, not reproducible.

name: Theatre and pantomime
note: Live performance of narrative. Ephemeral, audience present, not reproducible.

name: Woodblock carving
note: Hand-carved relief block prints many copies. First cheap reproducible image. Breaks scribe monopoly.

name: Relief printing
note: Ink raised surface, press down. Works with carbon ink and soft brush on absorbent surface.

name: Hand papermaking
note: Rag fibre beaten, suspended in water, scooped on mould. One sheet at a time. Variable thickness.

name: Water-driven pulp stamper
note: Water wheel drives cam-driven hammers beating rags. Faster, consistent pulp. Essential for volume.

name: Surface sizing
note: Alum and gelatin seal fibre. Ink sits on surface instead of bleeding through. Required for printing.

name: Wire mould and deckle
note: Fine brass wire mesh and wooden deckle frame. Allows consistent sheet thickness. Wire spacing visible.

name: Fourdrinier papermaking machine
note: Steam-driven endless wire belt. Pulp fed continuously. Thousands of tonnes per year. Displaces hand workers.

name: Wood pulp from timber
note: Wood fibres liberated by heat and alkali. Cheaper than rag pulp. Contains lignin, yellows and becomes brittle.

name: Oil-based printing ink
note: Carbon in heated linseed oil. Sticks to metal type. Water-based ink beads off metal, non-obvious blocker.

name: Type punch
note: Hardened steel letter in relief, hand-struck into soft matrix. Repeated use creates identical matrices.

name: Type matrix
note: Soft brass struck by hardened punch. Cavity is negative of letter. Reusable mould for casting type.

name: Adjustable hand mould
note: Iron mould with adjustable sides, matrix fitted into bottom. One caster casts thousands of identical sorts per day.

name: Type metal alloy
note: Lead and tin melt at low temp. Antimony is key: it expands on cooling, forcing alloy into matrix cavity edge.

name: Composing stick and galley
note: Compositors set metal sorts in stick, proof, transfer to galley. Allows rearrangement before lock-up.

name: Platen press
note: Flat bed with screwed platen pressing it down. Requires oil ink and level surfaces. Gutenberg innovation.

name: Cylinder press
note: Rotating cylinder instead of platen. Type moves under rolling pressure. Faster, smoother. Steam power essential.

name: Rotary press
note: Two cylinders, type wraps around curved plate. Continuous feed and output. Thousands of sheets per hour.

name: Stereotype plate
note: Plaster impression of type. Molten type poured into mould. Reusable, faster than resetting type.

name: Electrotype plate
note: Electroplated copper shell on lead backing. Sharper impression. More durable. Expensive.

name: Linotype machine
note: Operator taps keyboard, matrices drop, spacing added, hot metal poured into mould. Complete line emerges cast solid.

name: Monotype machine
note: Punched paper tape controls type casting. Each character cast individually. Slower than Linotype but flexible fonts.

name: Intaglio engraving
note: Furrows cut into copper plate. Ink fills grooves, wiped surface clean. Pressure forces paper into grooves. Fine detail.

name: Etching with acid
note: Wax ground on copper, needle drawn, acid bites. Tonal work without hand-cutting. Faster than engraving.

name: Lithography
note: Greasy ink on stone, water-acidified alum applied. Water repels grease, grease rejects water. Non-obvious chemistry.

name: Offset lithography
note: Image transfers to rubber roller, then paper. Multiple passes with less wear. Finer detail, longer plate life.

name: Halftone screening
note: THE invention making photographs printable. Cross-ruled screen photographed with image. Variable dots create tone illusion.

name: Four-colour separation
note: Cyan, magenta, yellow, black separations photographed through filters. Overprinted recreate full colour.

name: Newspaper institution
note: Daily publication breaks state monopoly on information. Political instrument. Cheap accurate copying enables rapid idea spread.

name: Typewriter
note: Keyed strike-through ribbon. QWERTY deliberately slows typist to prevent jams. Shift key accesses capitals.

name: Silver halide chemistry
note: Silver nitrate and sodium chloride form photosensitive silver chloride crystals. Darkens on exposure. Foundation of photography.

name: Daguerreotype plate
note: Polished copper plate, silver-coated, exposed to light, developed in mercury vapour. Mirror-like image. Cannot be copied.

name: Calotype negative-positive
note: The negative is the invention. Paper negative allows unlimited prints from one exposure. Cheaper than daguerreotype.

name: Wet collodion plate
note: Glass plate coated with collodion. Exposed wet. Huge leap in sensitivity and speed. Must develop within minutes.

name: Gelatin dry plate
note: Silver halide in gelatin. Sensitive when dry. Long shelf life. Easy storage and transport. Portable photography practical.

name: Roll film on celluloid
note: Flexible base allows compact cameras. Light and durable. Enables hand-held shooting. Photography becomes casual.

name: Optical enlarger
note: Light projects negative through lens onto sensitised paper. Magnification variable. Enlargement unlocks full potential.

name: Colour photography
note: Multi-layer emulsion sensitive to red, green, blue. Complex chemistry. Colour casts and fading persist. Natural colour possible.

name: Magic lantern projection
note: Candle or arc light projects painted glass slide through lens onto screen. Bright large image. Enables mass viewing.

name: Intermittent film movement
note: Sprockets and claw mechanism pull film frame-by-frame. Each frame holds still, advances in darkness. THE invention of cinema.

name: Cinema shutter
note: Rotating disc with opening blocks light during frame advance. Viewer sees each frame, not blur. Controls flicker.

name: Cinema projection
note: Arc lamp casts film frames through objective lens onto screen. Large bright image. Darkened theatre essential.

name: Film studio and stage
note: Large glass-roofed stage with strong arc lighting. Actors repeat scenes for camera. Raw material for film assembly.

name: Nitrate film storage safety
note: Nitrocellulose base extremely flammable and self-oxidising. Fires spontaneous and unstoppable. Underground vaults needed.

name: Phonograph with cylinder
note: Sound vibrates needle, etches waxy cylinder. Replay moves needle over groove, vibrates diaphragm. Sound reproduction.

name: Disc record and lateral recording
note: Groove meanders side-to-side encoding amplitude. Shellac pressing from master. Playable from multiple copies.

name: Loudspeaker
note: Coil in magnetic field vibrates diaphragm. Reverses microphone. Weak signal amplified for audible volume.

name: Electrical recording and amplification
note: Microphone captures sound, valve amplifier drives cutting stylus. Bass and treble accessible. Audio fidelity leap.

name: Magnetic wire and tape recording
note: Steel wire or tape magnetised by recording head. Erasable and reusable. Linear response superior to disc.

name: Radio broadcasting as medium
note: Sound broadcast live to distant unseen audiences. Electrical medium dissolves geography. State interest high.

name: Library and archive
note: Institutional preservation and organisation of texts. Enables distributed knowledge and cultural memory.

name: Cataloguing and classification
note: Systematic ordering by subject, author, title. Index cards or catalogue. Turns collection into resource.

name: Index and concordance
note: Complete list of every word and location. Enables rapid lookup and cross-reference. Transforms corpus to reference.

name: Copyright and publishing economics
note: Legal monopoly on copying enforces author and publisher income. Printing enables profitable copying.
